{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Sweden|Swedish recipes]]

'''Sockerdricka''' (Swedish for "sugar drink") is a soft drink from the 19th century. It is traditionally a [[Cookbook:Fermentation|fermented]] drink that contains ginger, but modern commercial versions consist of carbonated water, some sugar, and citric acid.

== Ingredients ==
* 20 [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* Peel of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 25 g [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* [[Cookbook:Raisin|Raisins]]

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the sugar, water, lemon and crushed ginger for 15 minutes. 
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the mixture and let it cool. 
# Mix in the yeast and let the mixture [[Cookbook:Fermentation|ferment]] for 2 days. 
# Put the drink in bottles, and add a raisin to each bottle.
# Cork the bottles, and let rest for 5 days. After 5 days the sockerdricka is ready for drinking.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* The recipe above has '''lots''' of yeast, and not much ginger. It would work well with just 10 g yeast. More ginger would be good (e.g. 100 g of fresh ginger for 20 litres).

==See also==
* [[Cookbook:Ginger beer|Ginger beer]]
* [[Cookbook:Sima|Sima]]
